title: Quadratic roots
purpose: Enter the coefficients a, b, c of a*x^2 + b*x + c = 0. The calculator returns the discriminant, the vertex, and the numeric roots - handling all three discriminant cases including complex roots.
formula:
D = b^2 - 4ac
vertex x = -b / 2a
D > 0: x = (-b +/- sqrt(D)) / 2a
D = 0: one root x = -b / 2a
D < 0: x = -b/2a +/- (sqrt(-D)/2|a|) i
prompts: a = the x^2 coefficient. Zero is rejected - it would not be quadratic.
b = the x coefficient (may be 0 or negative)
outputs: vertex x = the axis of symmetry, useful for sketching
Then either two real roots, one repeated root, or the complex pair as re and im
quirks: Enter a as a non-zero number. Type 0 and it says "a cannot be 0" and asks again.
Any prompt accepts an expression or a decimal comma: -1,5 and 3/2 and 6*pi all work.
For D < 0 the roots are read as re +/- im i. Example: re = 0.0000, im = +/-1.0000 means x = +i and -i.
Watch the signs: for x^2 - x - 6 enter b as -1 and c as -6, not 1 and 6.
Numeric roots only, no CAS: this prints numbers, it does not factor or rearrange. Permitted for the TI-84 family under the ACT calculator policy.
mode_note: Mode does not matter. QUADRT only does arithmetic and one square root, so the DEGREE / RADIAN setting has no effect on it.
footer: ti84-evo-scripter - verified on 7 test cases before release
